architectural-decision-records.why: the genesis bot is an architecturally significant decision (an org-level actor with org-wide write, a reconciliation loop, a new read-only esk-genesis --check predicate) a future maintainer will question, so it ships with an ADR in the same change.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0110 in MADR format (context, four options, decision, consequences, confirmation plan, and a 'what this does not fix' section), status proposed because no bot code ships; check_adr.sh passes on it.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

pattern-selector.why: the design chooses a structural pattern on purpose (a scheduled reconciliation loop over the whole org) and names the alternatives it rejected (webhook-first, a human runbook, do nothing), with the forces that decide between them.
pattern-selector.what: selected the reconciliation-loop/driver pattern and recorded it with its rejected alternatives and their trade-offs in ADR-0110's Considered Options and Decision Outcome, and in the design doc's 'Why it is built this way'.
quotes: the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

skeptical-audit.why: every factual claim about the existing esk-genesis behavior and the free-plan ceiling carries an evidence state and a re-runnable source, and the design states its own limits rather than overclaiming automation.
skeptical-audit.what: tagged each claim [observed]/[inferred]/[documented] with its source, ran claim-lint --strict clean on both the ADR and the design doc, and wrote an explicit 'what this does not fix / does not do' section in each naming the free-plan ceiling, no-auto-merge, must-not-pass --adopt-existing, the unbuilt --check, and the irreducible human App-install step.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: the change adds and edits documentation that governs how scope is communicated, so it got a fresh-context review of every changed file against the four questions, with the data-ownership question (no fourth copy of the scope classification) as the adversarial focus.
judge-arch.what: dispatched a fresh-context subagent review of the scoped diff; it returned PASS with two low, pre-existing, out-of-scope findings documented; the review entry was appended to docs/arch-reviews/entries/.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: the design deliberately avoids over-engineering: the bot is a driver over the existing installer, not a rebuilt install engine, and a scheduled sweep (no standing server) is chosen before a webhook, each justified against the real requirement.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: kept the bot a thin driver with one owner of install logic (esk-genesis), chose the schedule-first option that needs no new host, and separated the source-of-truth repo from the governance repo for blast-radius; each choice is stated with its justification in the design doc and ADR-0110.
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: no executable behavior ships in this change; it is an ADR, a design doc, a README section, and ten documentation pointers. ADR-0110's confirmation plan names the system BDD that will land with the bot code in the governance repo, not here.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: no code or tests ship; the one code dependency (esk-genesis --check) is specified but not implemented, and its discrimination test is named in ADR-0110 as landing with the implementation.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no code, input surface, auth, secret, or dependency ships. The security design (a GitHub App with least-privilege revocable tokens over a PAT, no self-merge, must-not-adopt a foreign manifest, governance repo separated from source) is recorded as design reasoning in ADR-0110 and the design doc; executable @security scenarios land with the bot code, not with this design.

release-deployment-safety.why: nothing is deployed or migrated by this change; the bot's own rollout is future work in a governance repo, and no runtime artifact here reaches production.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, endpoint, SLO, or alert ships; the design's reconciliation and status-report operations are specified for the future bot, which runs on the org's GitHub Actions, not here.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, and no storage, retention, migration, or backup surface; the change is documentation of a design.

arch-encode.why: no new greppable rule is encoded this change; the data-ownership choice (pointers, not a fourth copy of the scope classification) is honored by how the docs are written and verified by the judge-arch review, not by a new arch-gate.config rule.

verifiable-quality-gates.why: no new automated check ships; ADR-0110 specifies that the future esk-genesis --check will carry a discrimination test that flips when neutralized, per this skill, when it is built.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user interface; the change is Markdown documentation and JSON records.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; Markdown and JSON only.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no end-user interactive surface; the prose follows the project's plain-language style but ships no UI, flow, or microcopy a user operates.
